entry.title: The line-graph inertia conjecture
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $L(G)$ denote its line graph. Let $n^+(L(G))$ and $n^-(L(G))$ be the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $L(G)$, and let $s(L(G))$ be its signature. **Line-graph inertia conjecture.**

$$
n^+(L(G))\leq n^-(L(G))+1.
$$

Equivalently, $s(L(G))\leq 1$. The paper proves a weaker upper bound for line graphs and presents computational evidence for this sharper conjecture, which remains open.
entry.review_depth: source Conjecture 4.12, Theorem 4.13 use, dense-case remark read; exact counterexample computed; prior art abstract read
entry.disposition: Refuted, but already public. This lane independently found (by annealing, then exact verification) the connected 14-vertex, 16-edge cactus C5 - bridge - C4 (entered/left at adjacent vertices) - bridge - C5 with In(L(G)) = (9, 0, 7) by the integer characteristic polynomial and Descartes rule of signs (exact since all roots are real), and an infinite family C_{4a+1} - C_{4b} - C_{4c+1}. The identical 14-vertex cactus with inertia (9,0,7), a 48-vertex example and unbounded signature appear in arXiv:2607.22874 (v1 24 Jul 2026, v2 29 Jul 2026), "The signature of connected line graphs is unbounded" (also SSRN preprints by A. Paone). Zero credit. Side note: the source line "for any tree T, s(L(T)) <= -1" is false (L(P5) = P4 has signature 0); Guo theorem gives s <= 1, which still suffices for trees.

record.title: The reduced-graph order conjecture of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let a **reduced graph** mean a graph with no pair of vertices that can be removed without changing the relevant adjacency-matrix rank. Write $m(r)$ for

$$
m(r)=\begin{cases}2^{(r+2)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is even},\\5\cdot2^{(r-3)/2}-2&\text{if }r\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$
 **Akbari–Cameron–Khosrovshahi conjecture.** The order of any reduced graph of rank $r$ is at most $m(r)$. This conjecture is presented as a bound on the order of reduced graphs in terms of adjacency-matrix rank; the paper cites it as a proposal of Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi, without giving a resolution.
record.source_name: Saieed Akbari, Clive Elphick, Hitesh Kumar, Shivaramakrishna Pragada and Quanyu Tang, “A new conjecture on the inertia of graphs”, arXiv:2508.01163 (2025).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2103.13489](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.13489), [arXiv:1201.3060](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.3060).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01163

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2025).

entry.title: He–Juškevičius–Narayanan–Spiro conjecture for odd planar Rademacher sums
entry.statement:
Let $v_1,\dotsc,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be unit vectors, and let $\varepsilon_1,\dotsc,\varepsilon_n$ be independent random signs, each uniformly distributed in $\{-1,1\}$. **He–Juškevičius–Narayanan–Spiro conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that, for every odd $n$,

$$
\mathbb{P}\!\left[\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n\varepsilon_i v_i\right\|_2\leq 1\right]\geq\frac{c}{n}.
$$

This is the proposed odd-$n$ case of Erdős's conjecture, motivated by the fact that the known obstruction requiring radius $\sqrt{2}$ works only for even $n$; whether the asserted lower bound holds remains open in the supplied text.

entry.title: Schmeichel–Hakimi conjecture on exceptional planar graphical sequences
entry.exact_statement: A graphical sequence is **planar graphical** if it is the degree sequence of a planar graph. Using the shorthand $a^bc^d$ for $b$ repetitions of $a$ followed by $d$ repetitions of $c$, consider the sequences $5^{13}3^1$, $7^15^{17}$, and $7^35^{17}$. **Schmeichel–Hakimi conjecture.** None of these three sequences is planar graphical. The source states that these are the three unresolved cases remaining after their theorem, so the conjecture is open.

entry.title: The Graph Complement Conjecture for minimum rank
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Write $G^c$ for its complement, $\operatorname{mr}(G)$ for the minimum rank of a real symmetric matrix described by $G$, and $\ord G$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**Graph Complement Conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{mr}(G)+\operatorname{mr}(G^c)\leq \ord G+2.
$$

This is a classical Nordhaus–Gaddum-type conjecture in minimum rank theory; the bound is sharp for paths, but the source gives no resolution in general.

entry.title: The positive semidefinite Graph Complement Conjecture
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\operatorname{mr}_+(G)$ denote the minimum rank among positive semidefinite matrices in the class $\mathcal{S}(G)$ of real symmetric matrices described by $G$. Write $G^c$ for the complement of $G$ and $\ord G$ for its number of vertices.

**Positive semidefinite Graph Complement Conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{mr}_+(G)+\operatorname{mr}_+(G^c)\leq \ord G+2.
$$

This strengthens the ordinary Graph Complement Conjecture, and the source notes that the bound is sharp for paths; no general resolution is supplied.

entry.title: The Graph Complement Conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter $\nu$
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $G^c$ be its complement, and let $\nu(G)$ be the maximum nullity among positive semidefinite matrices in $\mathcal{S}(G)$ satisfying the Strong Arnold property. Let $\ord G$ denote the number of vertices of $G$.

**Graph Complement Conjecture for $\nu$.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\nu(G)+\nu(G^c)\geq \ord G-2.
$$

The inequality is stronger than the corresponding minimum-rank conjectures because $\nu(G)\leq \operatorname{M}_+(G)\leq \operatorname{M}(G)$. The source gives no general resolution here, although later results in the paper establish conditional bounds.

entry.title: The strong $\delta$-conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree, let $l(G)$ be its degeneracy,

$$
l(G)=\max\\{\delta(H):H\text{ is a subgraph of }G\\},
$$

let $\lceil\delta\rceil(G)$ be the maximum of $\delta(H)$ over minors $H$ of $G$, and let $\nu(G)$ be the positive semidefinite Colin de Verdière parameter.

**Strong $\delta$-conjecture for $\nu$.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\delta(G)\leq l(G)\leq \lceil\delta\rceil(G)\leq \nu(G).
$$

The first two inequalities follow directly from the definitions, while the conjectural content is the final inequality. The source later says that the corresponding original $\delta$-conjecture is used conditionally and does not supply a resolution of this full chain in the candidate span.

entry.title: Odd-minor Duchet–Meyniel conjecture of Ji, Song, Weiss, and Zhang
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, and let $oh(G)$ be the largest integer $\ell$ such that $G$ has an odd $K_\ell$ minor.

**Odd-minor Duchet–Meyniel conjecture.** For any graph $G$ of order $n$,

$$
oh(G)\geq \left\lceil\frac{n}{\alpha(G)}\right\rceil.
$$

This is the odd-minor analogue of the Duchet–Meyniel conjecture and is stronger than the corresponding lower bound obtained by replacing $oh(G)$ with the ordinary minor parameter. The source does not state whether it has been resolved.

entry.title: Heawood graph uniqueness conjecture for cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic bipartite graphs
entry.statement:
A graph is **2-factor Hamiltonian** if every 2-factor is a Hamiltonian cycle. A cubic graph is **cyclically 4-edge-connected** if every edge-cut whose removal leaves two components each containing a cycle has size at least 4. The Heawood graph is a cubic bipartite graph of girth 6.

**Heawood graph uniqueness conjecture.** The Heawood graph is the only 2-factor Hamiltonian cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic bipartite graph of girth at least 6.

This condition would suffice to prove the preceding classification conjecture, because a counterexample after repeated 3-cut reductions would be cyclically 4-edge-connected and have girth at least 6. The supplied text gives no resolution of this equivalent formulation.

entry.title: Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's classification conjecture for 2-factor Hamiltonian regular bipartite graphs
entry.literal_statement:
A **2-factor** of a graph is a 2-regular spanning subgraph, and a graph is **2-factor Hamiltonian** if every 2-factor is a Hamiltonian cycle. A **star product** of cubic graphs is the operation that deletes one degree-3 vertex from each graph and joins the resulting three pairs of neighbours. Let $G$ be a 2-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graph.

**Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's conjecture.** Either $k=2$ and $G$ is a cycle, or $k=3$ and $G$ can be obtained from $K_{3,3}$ and the Heawood graph $H_0$ by repeated star products.

The cited work proved that no such graphs exist for $k\geq 4$ and established additional structural restrictions for $k=3$, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the classification conjecture itself.

full_parsed_record.title: Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's classification conjecture for 2-factor Hamiltonian regular bipartite graphs
full_parsed_record.statement:
A **2-factor** of a graph is a 2-regular spanning subgraph, and a graph is **2-factor Hamiltonian** if every 2-factor is a Hamiltonian cycle. A **star product** of cubic graphs is the operation that deletes one degree-3 vertex from each graph and joins the resulting three pairs of neighbours. Let $G$ be a 2-factor Hamiltonian $k$-regular bipartite graph.

**Fleischner–Jackson–Litsyn–Swart's conjecture.** Either $k=2$ and $G$ is a cycle, or $k=3$ and $G$ can be obtained from $K_{3,3}$ and the Heawood graph $H_0$ by repeated star products.

The cited work proved that no such graphs exist for $k\geq 4$ and established additional structural restrictions for $k=3$, but the supplied text gives no resolution of the classification conjecture itself.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Marien Abreu, Jan Goedgebeur, Jorik Jooken, Federico Romaniello and Tibo Van den Eede, “The Gray graph is pseudo 2-factor isomorphic”, arXiv:2504.12095 (2026).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.12095

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2025). “This conjecture was disproved by Goedgebeur [Discr.\ Appl.\ Math.\ 193 (2015) 57--60] who constructed a counterexample $\mathcal{G}$ (of girth 6) on 30 vertices.”

entry.actual_review_depth: Conjecture 1.1, star-product definition and equivalence/brace discussion read.
entry.ordinary_attempt_and_precise_gap_or_excl: Star-product closure only constructs members. Splitting a cyclic 3-edge-cut reduces a potential counterexample, but one must exclude every other cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic brace. Pseudo-2-factor-isomorphic counterexamples do not refute 2-factor Hamiltonicity. Low degree vacuity only gives an excluded domain correction.

entry.title: The $K_7^{=}$-minor 6-colorability conjecture
entry.literal_statement:
Let $K_7^{=}$ be the graph obtained from the complete graph $K_7$ by deleting two edges. A graph is **$K_7^{=}$-minor-free** if it has no minor isomorphic to $K_7^{=}$.

**$K_7^{=}$-minor 6-colorability conjecture.** Every graph with no $K_7^{=}$-minor is $6$-colorable.

This is proposed as the symmetrical counterpart to the paper's proved result for $K_7^{\vee}$, where the two deleted edges have a common end. The conjecture is presented as open, and the source notes that an appropriate extremal theorem is still missing.
entry.ordinary_attempt_and_exact_gap: Source distinguishes independent deleted edges K7-equals from incident deleted edges K7-vee. The latter 6-colorability theorem is not a proof of the former. Need the extremal/contraction-critical argument for independent-edge deletion; no explicit 7-chromatic counterexample or full proof found.

entry.title: Seymour's epsilon conjecture for graphs with independence number two
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\operatorname{had}(G)$ be its Hadwiger number. **Seymour's epsilon conjecture.** There is a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ satisfies 
$$
\operatorname{had}(G)\geqslant\left(\frac13+\varepsilon\right)|V(G)|.
$$
 This conjecture asks for any improvement over the classical $|V(G)|/3$ lower bound and is presented as an open problem.
entry.ordinary_attempt_and_exact_gap: Source Conjecture 5 repeats the epsilon statement. Complete equivalence to 371754 saved in ordinary notes. Examples satisfying stronger Hadwiger bounds do not produce a common epsilon for every alpha=2 graph. Duplicate endpoint receives no separate candidate or credit.
